new_primary_supplement.text_limitation: Math-font extraction contains corrupt glyphs. The equation descriptions below were checked against rendered page images, not guessed from extracted symbols.

verified_findings.finding: Subinterval coordinate transformations enable pulse pre-elimination from reduced normal equations. Pulse constraints enter before elimination; cross-epoch constraints require a modified step.
Elimination retains weighted residual energy and supports final-state covariance; backward substitution then recovers earlier parameters.
Epoch clocks and phase biases have distinct elimination lifetimes; additional parameters are explicitly partitioned into retained and eliminable groups.
An algebraic-equivalence experiment reports about 0.5 mm/day along-track drift, below 1 mm/day in observed cases, and radial/cross-track differences below 0.05 mm.
The rapid method recovers parameter standard deviations and some covariance blocks, not the complete covariance. Connected ambiguity sets inform datum selection.

new_primary_supplement.interpretation_for_our_work: Subinterval elimination, nuisance lifetimes, residual-energy retention, and numerical-equivalence comparisons have direct precedent. Our square-root implementation and strict checks are engineering differences requiring measured evidence; this review establishes no first-of-kind claim.

decision.new_evidence: Primary equation-level supplement now available for the reduced-dynamic elimination family.
decision.paper_position: Continue positioning the work as a prospective controlled scientific comparison, with honest uncertainty and failure reporting. Do not claim Gauss-Markov density estimation or segmented orbit elimination as new, or claim other methods lack an unexamined feature.
decision.smallest_follow_up: Obtain the exact two articles through a legitimate accessible author copy or existing institutional/library access; compare Li's state/prior/nuisance definitions before asserting scientific differentiation. The dissertation already warrants explicit related-work treatment when the manuscript is next edited.
